title: Rudolf Kálmán and the Control-Theory Origin of 'Observability' (1960)
explainer: In 1960, engineer Rudolf Kálmán introduced 'observability' as a precise concept in control theory: a system is observable if its complete internal state can be reconstructed purely from watching its external outputs over time. Software observability borrows this exact idea almost unchanged - metrics, logs, and traces are the 'outputs' engineers use to infer what's happening inside a system too complex to inspect directly. The term predates web services by decades; it was first used to analyze spacecraft and industrial control systems, not microservices.
